frames.narration: The customer presses Pay. The page sends the order and a fresh idempotency key, order-81-1. The card number went straight from the provider's card form to the provider; the shop only holds a token.
Before calling the provider, the API saves the payment in the processing state under that key. If the server crashed right now, a recovery job would find this row.
The API asks the provider to charge the token and passes the same key along. The provider charges the card, but the reply is lost on the way back.
The API does not know if the card was charged. It does not guess. It retries once with the same key, and the provider sees a key it has already handled and returns the charge it already made.
The charge succeeded. In one database transaction the API marks pay_1 succeeded, writes a debit and a credit of 25.99 to the ledger, and writes an event row to the outbox.
The customer is shown the result. The outbox relay publishes the payment event and the order service marks the order as paid.
The provider also sends its own signed webhook. The handler checks the signature, sees the payment is already succeeded and changes nothing. A repeat is harmless.
Overnight the provider's settlement report is matched against the ledger. Every charge has a payment with the same key and amount, so the day reconciles with nothing to fix.
